summary: Three pre-event runs against the real memoff harness: one smoke (orchestration only, 2 issues), one small real run (2 issues, claude-haiku-5-5, all passed), one full real run (8 issues, same model). Recall fired correctly on every issue from issue 2 onward in the full run (1 item, 8000 chars each), confirmed via a fixed receipt.sh. Clearest controlled helped case: a standalone selftest where the agent answered a question correctly using only recalled context, never stated in the prompt. Clearest gap: issues 2-8 of the full run did not meet their exact visible-failure targets -- a claude-haiku-5-5 correctness limit, not a memory failure; recall itself succeeded on all of them. The one number for a judge: 8/8 issues got a non-empty, correctly-scoped recall from issue 2 onward, at $2.29 total measured agent cost across the full 8-issue chain.
scorecard: n/a - our entrant is not the cognee-memory@cognee plugin; that plugin's own background instrumentation was present (v1.7.1, installed for its cognee-report skill dependency) but is not a measurement of our system and is not reported here

full_run_cumulative.memory_cost_usd_note: null per-issue by design; usage.sh reports a character-count estimate only, cost_usd explicitly null -- cognee's REST API has no public per-call usage endpoint found; declared gap, not hidden
full_run_cumulative.total_cost_usd_note: display quirk: harness reports 0 at cumulative level despite real nonzero agent_cost_usd, because memory_cost_usd is explicitly unmeasured (null) per issue; agent_cost_usd is the trustworthy figure

what_did_not_work: Receipt-reporting bug, found and fixed: MEMOFF_STATE_DIR never reaches wait.sh/receipt.sh/usage.sh (confirmed by reading sequencer.py), only the hook inside the claude subprocess. Fixed by anchoring on MEMOFF_INJECTED_DIR instead; re-validated against the real sequencer twice.

Correctness gate not met for issues 2-8 of the full run (visible-failure counts above target, e.g. issue 8: 1 failed vs target 0). claude-haiku-5-5 was a cost choice for pre-event testing; recall itself fired correctly on every one of these issues.

Dataset contamination during ad hoc testing, not a submission bug: an un-wiped leftover dataset from an earlier manual test leaked into a later unrelated recall query. Traced to a testing-hygiene gap, not a flaw in cognee's recall filtering or in wipe.sh/wipe_check.sh, both separately re-verified correct against the real harness.
